what_worked: Clear audience framing for indie hackers with actionable decision filters and category comparisons.
fix_next: Multiple median values diverge from reference data (Education, Marketing, Analytics, AI, B2B/B2C ratio); verify calculations against raw dataset before presenting.
verdict: Competent overview with useful framing but too many numerical inaccuracies.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: Total MRR $13.5M — dataset gives 30-day revenue $15.6M, unclear derivation; $134M '12-mo revenue' appears fabricated (no annualized field in dataset). Slide 4: Education median $2,142 vs reference $2,435; Marketing $1,586 vs $2,369.50; Analytics $1,294 vs $419; AI $446 vs $503; SaaS $303 vs $200.50 — mixed accuracy, Analytics is wildly off. Slide 6: 197 startups at $0 vs reference 216 zero-revenue. Slide 7: B2B/B2C 5.7x ratio claimed ($1,036/$181) — reference shows ~2.35x median revenue multiple for B2B; the absolute medians and ratio don't match reference. Slide 8: Stripe total MRR $11.7M vs reference $13.5M; Dodo $12.7k vs reference $38.7k. Slide 12: 'Stripe processes 87% of all MRR' — reference shows $13.5M/$15.6M = 86.7%, close but the $11.7M on slide 8 contradicts this.

evidence.insight: Slide 11 synthesizes categories into high-MRR vs crowded buckets with screening criteria — goes beyond chart description. Slide 9 highlights growth-filtered acquisition targets. However, insights remain surface-level: no cross-cutting analysis (e.g., category × audience type, anonymity premium).
evidence.narrative: Flows logically: snapshot → categories → geography → distribution → B2B/B2C → payments → growth → acquisitions → recommendations. But reads as a tour of dimensions rather than building toward a single thesis. The 'landing' on slide 12 is a recap list, not a synthesized argument.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 clearly targets indie hackers. Scope and date are stated. However, 274 missing category values and 288 missing audience_type values are never disclosed, which materially affects category and B2B/B2C analyses. No limitations slide.
evidence.accuracy: Multiple median values diverge from reference: Education off by ~$300, Marketing off by ~$780, Analytics off by ~$875, B2B/B2C ratio inflated from ~2.35x to 5.7x. Zero-revenue count 197 vs 216. Dodo Payments total revenue $12.7k vs $38.7k. Stripe total MRR internally inconsistent ($11.7M on slide 8 vs 87% claim on slide 12). The $134M '12-mo revenue' has no dataset basis.
evidence.visual: Clean, consistent dark/light theme alternation. Bar charts are well-labeled and appropriately chosen. Card-based layouts on slides 5, 8, 10 are legible. Color coding is purposeful (green highlights, category differentiation). Slide 6 distribution visualization is creative. Minor issue: bar lengths on slide 6 don't proportionally represent counts.
evidence.ai_slop: Minimal filler language. Slide design is template-consistent but not generic. No decorative-but-meaningless graphics. The deck avoids consulting jargon. Slight concern: the uniformity of layout suggests AI generation but quality is maintained.
